data.title: DIS Stock Breaks Above $125 For First Time Since 2022: Disney Retail Bulls Are Talking About A ‘Santa Claus Rally’
data.summary: Several factors help optimism around Disney. Its theme parks business continues to grow profits, while its streaming operations are becoming more profitable ahead of Hulu's planned full integration into Disney+ in December. Disney plans to spend more on content in fiscal 2027, with spending expected to reach about $26 billion, up 9% from fiscal 2026. It expects operating income to rise by high-single digits in Entertainment and Experiences and by double digits in Sports. [...] Disney Stock Hits Four-Year High As Theme Parks, Streaming Drive Optimism Walt Disney's stock broke above the $125 level on Wednesday, reaching an intraday high of $126.28, its highest level in four years, before closing at $125.60. The gains extend a rally following Disney's better-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter results earlier this month. [...] Walt Disney Co. (DIS) stock reached above $125, hitting its highest level since 2022, as retail investors grew hopeful of a potential Santa Claus rally. A federal judge's halt on FCC's (Federal Communications Commission) license reviews for eight ABC-owned stations added to the optimism. Walt Disney stock edged 0.3% higher overnight Wednesday, after a 2% gain in regular session. The stock is also headed for its best month since May 2025.

data.title: Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro Unifies AI Under CTO Karandeep Anand | Business Chief
data.summary: Josh D’Amaro, CEO of The Walt Disney Company, now wants every division running on one standard AI system, overseen by Karandeep Anand, the company’s first-ever Chief Technology Officer. “We see AI as a real tailwind for experiences,” Josh tells investors on Disney’s fiscal fourth-quarter call. [...] - Disney is replacing division-level AI tools with one standard system under CTO Karandeep Anand, who joined in September 2026 - Managers have reportedly been told to target 20% annual cost savings - Disney aims for US$3bn in annual run-rate savings by fiscal 2029, to be reinvested in content and technology - Nearly half of Disney’s new ad campaigns now run through an agentic AI tool Disney Hires Former Character.ai CEO Karandeep Anand as Its First CTO [...] Managers have reportedly been told to aim for 20% in annual cost savings. Disney expects US$3bn in annual run-rate savings by fiscal 2029, all of it reinvested in content and technology. Raymond Wang, a Constellation Research consultant who works with Disney, says the efficiency drive is overdue. “Disney’s been bloated for some time,” he says. “It’s because they wanted to preserve the culture of all their acquisitions.”
